idiom_name: List[Message => Either[StepError, Message]] folded with foldLeft (Function1.andThen for the pure form)
implementation_notes: Scala's function values make the slip a List[Message => Either[StepError, Message]] folded with foldLeft (or a traverse from Cats for effectful steps), and Function1.andThen composes the same steps into one function when no progress marker is needed - the Router/Step class hierarchy disappears into function composition. Keeping the index or an Either accumulator is what makes the flow resumable and failures data instead of exceptions. Akka/Pekko Streams and workflow libraries are the runtime cousins for streaming or distributed flows, but their topologies are assembled at startup, so they do not carry per-message itineraries. Retain a trait-based Step only when steps need dependency injection.
pitfalls: foldLeft keeps no position, so a Left loses how far the message travelled; thread an index or use an EitherT/stateful accumulator when retries must resume.
Functions in case classes break serialization for Akka remoting or JSON: send step ids and resolve them through a registry, never the lambdas.
Future- or IO-based steps hide partial completion; the effects of already-run steps are not rolled back, so compensation must be part of the step design.
Exceptions thrown inside a map/flatMap chain bypass Either and abort the flow with the cursor unrecorded - wrap foreign code with Try and convert.
